testsAdded.why: No test pinned track's `closing` check, the code that makes Close's drain bound absolute. With the check disabled (`if false && p.closing`), the implementer's sessionproxy and launcher suites both still passed. A connection whose upstream dial lands after Close has begun is then copied for until the drain runs out, and one landing after the force-close escapes it and holds Close forever. The new test passes at head (5 runs; 5 more under -race) and fails under that mutation (`the upstream's connection is still open`). It is a regression lock on correct code, not a red test: the code is right.

budgetCheck: The daemon's start wait is `starting = deadline + terminationGrace` (relaunch.go). `deadline` is the fixed launcher-connection deadline, start + bootTimeout, by which the launcher must already be connected, and --stop-grace is terminationGrace (manifest.go:478). So when the wait begins at least one full grace remains, and StopGrace/2 for the proof fits inside it. That holds less any time recordAddresses, or a stop of a stale earlier generation, takes before the Start is sent. A stale generation means a connected launcher, which is normally early, so this narrows only an edge case.
